title: I’m making DUNSPIN, a roguelike autobattler with hero builds and deckbuilding
author: Tap_Little
selftext:
DUNSPIN combines hero upgrades, equipment builds, and card deckbuilding. You recruit heroes and buy gear from the reels, merge duplicates, and build your deck around your party’s synergies to take on bosses.



Before each battle, you recruit heroes, equip them, and choose which cards to play. Three copies of the same hero at the same rank merge into a stronger one, up to 3 stars. Once your party is ready, the fight plays out automatically.



There are 60 heroes across 6 classes and 20 origins, giving you 26 types of synergy to build around. Field different heroes with matching traits to activate bonuses. You can focus on a few synergies or mix several together, depending on what you find.



Equipment helps shape each hero’s role. You can make them tougher, speed up their attacks, or add effects like burn and poison. Matching those effects with your cards gives you more ways to build your party.



Your deck develops throughout the run, with over 100 cards to choose from. You normally draw five cards and have three energy each round, so you have to choose what matters most for the next fight. You can add cards, upgrade them, and remove ones that no longer fit your build.



I’m using Claude and Codex for coding, along with AI tools for art and music. One thing I’ve had to keep revising is visual consistency: small details that looked fine in individual assets often looked messy in the actual game, so I kept simplifying shapes and adjusting outlines.



Does the trailer make it clear how the party builds and cards work together?



The demo has been submitted to Steam for review and isn’t publicly available yet.
